A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons cover all 20 pages, including Appendices A–G, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original multilingual GPT-2 experiments, including perplexity and generalization results in Figures 1–4, replication and tokenizer experiments in Appendices A–B, and statistical results in Appendix G.

after.justification: v4 retains these original multilingual experiments and their results in Figures 1–6 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: The GPT-2 small architecture, tokenization approach, sentence perturbations, and NP manipulation procedures are unchanged in Sections 3–6 and the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same OPUS12/OPUS30 data, BabyLM replication data, 12-language comparisons, and four-language NP-order experiments. Correcting the Portuguese label does not change language coverage.

E2.justification: Attested controls, impossible-language variants, NP_RANDOM, and the appendix replication conditions retain the same membership in their corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported protocols are identical, including the 10K-sentence perplexity evaluation, 1,200-step main training budget, 120 warmup steps, 10-fold SVM evaluation, and final-checkpoint minimal-pair test.

E4.justification: The replication checks, tokenizer vocabulary-size pilot, TCW correlation analysis, and NP generalization analysis are retained without additions or revisions.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three-seed experiments, 95% confidence intervals, quartile reporting for the tokenizer pilot, correlation tests, and Bonferroni-adjusted Welch tests. Appendix G is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted data are unchanged, including SVM macro F1 of 0.75 with SD 0.08, Figures 1–6, and the appendix significance tables. Figure 3 changes only a language-name spelling.

T1.justification: The GenScore and ΔGenScore definitions in Section 6, including Equation 1, are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about partial separation of attested and impossible languages and differing perplexity versus generalization evidence for human-like learning biases.

C2.justification: The randomness and constituency explanations, entropy-confound discussion, and qualifications concerning model size, data size, linguistic coverage, and corpus noise remain unchanged in Sections 6.2–8.

D1.justification: Training details, tokenizer specifications, parser/POS mappings, GPU and runtime disclosures, and code/data access information are identical. The updated arXiv version link adds no reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to Kallini et al. (2024), Xu et al. (2025), and other prior research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The byline expands 'Ethan Wilcox' to 'Ethan Gotlieb Wilcox', the arXiv version/date stamp is updated, and Figure 3 corrects 'Portugueseh' to 'Portuguese'. The prose and section structure otherwise remain identical.

P2.justification: Figure 3 corrects the Portuguese panel heading, and the longer author name slightly changes byline spacing. Figure contents, axes, legends, captions, tables, and the remaining page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 expands an author name and corrects an obvious spelling error in Figure 3, alongside the version/date update. This minor editorial polish leaves the scientific content, evidence, reproducibility, and substantive clarity unchanged.
